datasets.name: RapidEye satellite imagery
datasets.verbatim: This work used the RapidEye 3A product (orthorectified, radiometric, and geometric corrections) and was acquired from the Planet Explorer website [79].

datasets.name: Shuttle Radar Topography Mission (SRTM) 1 arc-second global (30 m) DEM
datasets.verbatim: The SRTM acquired interferometric radar data with dual antennas and provided data with 1 arc-second (30 m) spatial resolution... The SRTM product was the 1 arc-second global (30 m).

datasets.name: Landslide inventory (Nova Friburgo, Teresópolis, Rolante)
datasets.source: Authors' interpretation validated with Coelho-Netto et al. [10] and Uehara et al. [75]
datasets.verbatim: The landslides were interpreted from the RapidEye and Google Earth Pro version 7.3 imagery and validated with [10,75] to minimize interpretation errors.

methods.name: U-Net
methods.summary: A fully convolutional encoder-decoder architecture with convolutional layers, max-pooling, dropout, and up-sampling, trained using Binary Cross Entropy and the Adam optimizer to produce a binary landslide mask.
methods.source: Soares, L.P.; Dias, H.C.; Garcia, G.P.B.; Grohmann, C.H.
methods.verbatim: The code used in this research is available at the following link: https://github.com/SPAMLab/data_sharing/tree/main/Landslide_Segmentation_with_Deep_Learning_Evaluating_Model_Generalization_in_Rainfall-Induced_Landslides_in_Brazil

data_links.name: Landslide inventory GIS data used in SPAMLab projects (may include Brazil paper's inventories)

code_links.name: U-Net deep learning code for landslide segmentation and model generalization evaluation (Brazil)
code_links.summary: Code accompanying the paper, implementing the U-Net-based landslide segmentation pipeline used to evaluate model generalization on rainfall-induced landslides across three test areas in Brazil.
code_links.source: Soares, Dias, Garcia, Grohmann, 2022, Remote Sensing, DOI: 10.3390/rs14092237

availability.author_statement: Full data and code availability statement, with shared links.

reproducibility_assessment: The landslide inventory is linked via the SPAMLab repository, and input datasets are accessible through standard public providers (SRTM) or referenced sources (RapidEye). The custom U-Net code is available via a persistent GitHub and Codeberg repository link.
